semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Instance segmentation is a subtask of image segmentation focused on identifying each instance of objects within images. Thus, while related, they aren't equivalent.

parent_domains.justification: Instance segmentation is a specialized task under the broader category of segmentation.
Instance segmentation is a subtype of image segmentation, focusing on identifying and delineating each distinct object in an image.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Image segmentation is the closest parent domain because instance segmentation is directly concerned with segmenting images at a finer granularity than general segmentation.

child_domains.justification: Brain tumor segmentation is a specific application of instance segmentation in the medical field.

closest_child_domain.justification: Among the child domains, brain tumor segmentation is explicitly about segmenting instances of a particular object type, fitting most closely under instance segmentation.

sibling_domains.justification: Both semantic segmentation and instance segmentation fall under image segmentation and deal with segmenting images, albeit with different goals. Semantic focuses on categorizing pixels, while instance identifies individual objects.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Semantic segmentation is the closest sibling as it deals with segmenting images into different classes, similar to instance segmentation's focus on delineating individual objects.

unrelated_domains.justification: This domain relates more to identifying objects in an unsupervised manner, rather than segmenting known instances.

Medical image segmentation can encompass varying techniques beyond only instance segmentation, often focused on semantic level understanding.
